significance: Universally recognized as the birth of modern mountaineering, breaking centuries of mythological terror regarding high peaks.

climbers: Edward Whymper, Michel Croz, Lord Francis Douglas, Charles Hudson, Douglas Hadow, Peter Taugwalder Sr. & Jr.
significance: Marked the conclusion of the Golden Age of Alpinism, celebrated for triumph and sobered by tragic descent when a rope snapped.

event: First Ascent of an 8,000m Peak (Annapurna I)
significance: The first time human beings stood on the summit of an eight-thousander, accomplished without supplemental bottled oxygen.
Reaching the highest point on Earth along the Southeast Ridge via the South Col and Hillary Step.

event: First Ascent of K2 (The Savage Mountain)
climbers: Achille Compagnoni & Lino Lacedelli (Supported by Walter Bonatti & Amir Mehdi)
significance: Conquest of Earth's second-highest and notoriously steepest, most lethal peak via the Abruzzi Spur.

event: First Ascent of Everest Without Supplemental Oxygen
significance: Proved physiological feasibility of human respiration in the Death Zone without bottled oxygen, rewriting medical assumptions.

event: First Human to Climb All 14 Eight-Thousanders
significance: Messner completed all 14 peaks over 8,000m entirely without supplemental oxygen and largely in pure alpine style.

event: Historic First Winter Ascent of K2
climbers: Nirmal Purja, Mingma G, Gelje Sherpa, Mingma David Sherpa & Team
significance: Solved the 'Last Great Problem of High Altitude Mountaineering' under -60°C conditions, standing on the summit while singing the Nepali anthem.
